title: Safety Harness Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1910.140)
subtitle: For the inspection before initial use in each workshift, plus anchorage, rigging and rescue checks on site.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
Remove any defective component from service (1910.140(c)(18)). Equipment subjected to impact loading stays out of use until a competent person clears it (1910.140(c)(17)).
The manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Harness, lanyards and lifelines
items: No mildew, wear, damage or other deterioration on any strap, stitch line or rope
Not subjected to impact loading, or a competent person has inspected it and found it undamaged and safe
Full body harness in use; no body belt used as part of a personal fall arrest system
Knots in lanyards or vertical lifelines
Every knot inspected by a competent or qualified person before the line is used
No natural fiber rope used as a lifeline
Any polypropylene rope contains a UV light inhibitor
Lines and harness kept clear of anything that could cut, abrade or melt them
Equipment not used to hoist tools or materials

sections.title: Connectors: D-rings, snaphooks and carabiners
items: Corrosion-resistant finish; smooth surfaces and edges with nothing that could damage connected parts
Snaphooks and carabiners lock automatically and need two separate, consecutive movements to open
D-rings, snaphooks and carabiners rated to sustain at least 5,000 pounds (22.2 kN) tensile load
Not clipped directly to webbing, rope or wire rope, or the connector is designed for that
No snaphook or carabiner clipped to another, unless built for it
No connector added to a D-ring already holding another connector, unless designed for it
Only connectors designed for horizontal lifelines are attached to one
Connected object cannot press the gate open and let the parts separate
Ropes, belts, lanyards and harness match every connector used with them

sections.title: Anchorages and lifelines
items: Fall protection anchorage separate from any anchorage that suspends workers or platforms
Anchorage on an overhead member of the platform, above and near its center
Anchorage supports at least 5,000 pounds (22.2 kN) for each employee attached
Engineered anchorage (if not rated per employee)
Designed, installed and used under a qualified person's supervision, as part of a complete system with a safety factor of two or more
Designed, installed and used under the supervision of a qualified person
Horizontal lifeline that may become vertical
Connecting device locks in both directions on the lifeline

sections.title: Fit, rigging and rescue
items: Harness attachment point in the center of the back near shoulder level; chest point only where free fall is 2 feet (0.6 m) or less
Rigged so the worker cannot free fall more than 6 feet (1.8 m) or contact a lower level, unless the manufacturer exception in the clause is demonstrated
Strap configuration would hold the worker without contacting the neck and chin area
Arrangements for prompt rescue of each employee after a fall are in place for this job

sections.title: Window cleaners' positioning systems
items: Anchors with damaged or deteriorated fastenings or supports are removed, or their heads detached so they cannot be used
Anchor in the side frame or mullion, 42 to 51 inches (106.7 to 129.5 cm) above the sill
No rope in use with wear or deterioration that affects its strength
Each belt terminal on a separate window anchor during cleaning
At least one terminal attached before the worker climbs through the opening and until fully back inside
No snow, ice or other slippery condition; not weakened or rotted
Sill or ledge width and slope
At least 4 inches (10 cm) wide and sloping no more than 15 degrees below horizontal (steeper sills: see 1910.140(e)(2)(ix)(B))

references: 29 CFR 1910.140: Personal fall protection systems (Part 1910 Subpart I, Personal Protective Equipment)
disclaimer: General guidance only, not legal advice. Check the current regulation and your employer's procedures.
